question: m04
q: Is unemployment higher in NSW or Victoria right now, and by how much?

transcript.answer:
Unemployment is higher in Victoria. In September 2026, the latest month available, the seasonally adjusted rate was **5.1% in Victoria and 4.7% in NSW**. That's about **0.3 percentage points** higher in Victoria (5.05% vs 4.71%). Rounding each figure first makes the gap look like 0.4 points.

**The gap has narrowed quickly.** It was about 0.8 points in August and roughly 1.1 points in June. Most of the change came from NSW: its rate jumped from 4.35% in August to 4.71% in September. Victoria's dipped slightly, from 5.17% to 5.05%.

| Month (2026) | NSW | Victoria | Gap (Vic − NSW) |
|---|---|---|---|
| April | 4.42% | 4.85% | 0.42 pts |
| May | 4.33% | 4.90% | 0.57 pts |
| June | 3.97% | 5.12% | 1.14 pts |
| July | 4.27% | 5.11% | 0.84 pts |
| August | 4.35% | 5.17% | 0.81 pts |
| September | 4.71% | 5.05% | 0.34 pts |

State figures move around a lot from month to month because the survey samples are smaller than the national one. So don't read too much into NSW's September jump until the next few releases show whether it lasts.

*Source: ABS Labour Force, Australia, seasonally adjusted unemployment rate (persons).*
